title: RBI Minutes: Rate Cuts Off the Table as Inflation Risks Spread Beyond Food and Fuel
excerpt: Minutes of the RBI's October meeting show a unanimous 25-basis-point hike to 5.50% — the first in nearly four years — and a 4-2 split on shifting to 'calibrated tightening,' with Governor Sanjay Malhotra saying the next move can only be a hike or a pause.
body:
• The RBI's Monetary Policy Committee voted unanimously to raise the repo rate by 25 basis points to 5.50% at its October meeting — its first hike in nearly four years — the minutes released Wednesday show.
  • Governor Sanjay Malhotra: the shift to 'calibrated tightening' means 'rate cuts are off the table in the near term,' and the next move can only be a hike or a pause.
  • Retail inflation accelerated to 5.54% in September; the RBI raised its full-year forecast to 5.2% and expects inflation to average 6% in the October-December quarter.
  • For borrowers: two external members, Nagesh Kumar and Ram Singh, voted against the tighter stance, arguing inflation is supply-driven — but they were outvoted 4-2, so floating-rate borrowers should not expect EMI relief soon.

Members of India's rate-setting panel indicated that further rate hikes may be needed to curb inflation but stopped short of endorsing an aggressive tightening cycle, minutes of the Reserve Bank of India's October Monetary Policy Committee meeting showed on Wednesday.

The committee unanimously raised the repo rate by 25 basis points to 5.50% earlier this month, its first hike in nearly four years, and shifted its stance to "calibrated tightening" from "neutral" by a 4-2 vote, according to Reuters.

Why the Panel Turned

A sharp rise in oil prices due to the Middle East war and a deficient monsoon have driven up food prices. Retail inflation accelerated to a higher-than-expected 5.54% in September, nearing the RBI's 6% tolerance ceiling. The central bank raised its average inflation forecast for the current financial year to 5.2% from 5%, expects inflation to average 6% in the October-December quarter, and nudged its growth forecast up 40 basis points to 7.1%.

Malhotra pointed to broadening pressure: 37% of the commodities in the CPI basket had inflation above 4% in August, up from 20% in March, the minutes said, per PTI's account.

"Rate cuts are off the table in the near term and policy action ahead can only be a rate hike or a pause, depending on the evolving circumstances and the outlook."

— Sanjay Malhotra, RBI Governor, in the MPC minutes

Deputy Governor Poonam Gupta argued the panel should not wait for definitive evidence that price pressures are generalising, given monetary policy's lags: "It is conceivable that a further increase in the policy rate might be needed to keep inflation low and inflationary expectations anchored."

The Dissent

The two votes against the stance change came from external members Nagesh Kumar and Ram Singh. Kumar backed the 25-basis-point hike but said inflation "is driven largely by supply-side factors and does not show any signs of overheating of the economy nor of generalisation," favouring a neutral stance amid geopolitical and trade uncertainty. Singh warned that signalling calibrated tightening could imply an extended hiking cycle and undermine recent growth-supportive monetary and fiscal policies.

What Markets Expect

Traders have priced in a little over 100 basis points of hikes over the next 12 months, Reuters reported, and Goldman Sachs' text-based measure found the minutes more hawkish than Malhotra's policy statement. The practical translation for households and NRIs with India exposure is direct: borrowing costs in India are set to rise or stay high, deposit rates should remain firm, and any relief cycle is, in the governor's own framing, off the table until inflation's spread — not just its level — reverses.
